rules.text: Within the past 2 years have you: had a heart attack or aneurysm, or had or been medically advised to have any type of heart, brain or circulatory surgery (including, but not limited to a pacemaker insertion, defibrillator placement), or any procedure to improve circulation?
rules.note: VERIFIED_FROM_CARRIER_GUIDE via WebFetch (question text as returned by WebFetch from the guide's embedded application, p.9-10; spot-verify against the PDF). Replaces workbook paraphrase CQ: "Within 2 years: heart attack/aneurysm or heart, brain, or circulatory surgery/procedure including pacemaker/defibrillator or circulation procedure.". Workbook rows: CQ0008 [CURRENT_CARRIER_2026] https://www.fmiagent.com/wp-content/uploads/2026-07-14_American-Amicable_Golden_Solution_Whole_Life_Advisor_Guide_9507_3-26.pdf Guide p.9 / PDF p.8; CR0019 [CURRENT_CARRIER_2026] https://www.fmiagent.com/wp-content/uploads/2026-07-14_American-Amicable_Golden_Solution_Whole_Life_Advisor_Guide_9507_3-26.pdf Guide pp.9,40. 'heart, brain or circulatory surgery ... or any procedure to improve circulation' -> HEART_SURGERY, ANGIOPLASTY_STENT, PACEMAKER, DEFIBRILLATOR + proposed CIRCULATORY_SURGERY and BRAIN_SURGERY (no canonical code for non-cardiac circulatory or brain surgery). 'advised to have' surgery not yet done is also caught by Q6.

Replaces workbook paraphrase CQ: "Within 3 years: stroke, angina, heart attack, aneurysm, heart/circulatory surgery, or circulation procedure.". Workbook rows: CQ0011 [CURRENT_CARRIER_2026] https://www.fmiagent.com/wp-content/uploads/2026-07-14_American-Amicable_Golden_Solution_Whole_Life_Advisor_Guide_9507_3-26.pdf Guide p.9 / PDF p.8; CR0013 [CURRENT_CARRIER_2026] https://www.fmiagent.com/wp-content/uploads/2026-07-14_American-Amicable_Golden_Solution_Whole_Life_Advisor_Guide_9507_3-26.pdf Guide pp.9,40; CR0020 [CURRENT_CARRIER_2026] https://www.fmiagent.com/wp-content/uploads/2026-07-14_American-Amicable_Golden_Solution_Whole_Life_Advisor_Guide_9507_3-26.pdf Guide pp.9,40. TIA is NOT named in Q8a (only stroke); the Rx list agrees (Plavix/Coumadin 'Stroke/TIA/Heart Attack' at 2 years, 'Stroke/Heart Attack' at 3 years). Heart/circulatory surgery and procedures as in Q7b (brain surgery not named in Q8a).

rules.text: Within the past 3 years have you been medically diagnosed or treated, or hospitalized for: or taken medication for any form of cancer (excluding basal cell skin cancer), emphysema, chronic bronchitis, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), ulcerative colitis, cirrhosis, Hepatitis C, or liver disease?
rules.note: VERIFIED_FROM_CARRIER_GUIDE via WebFetch (question text as returned by WebFetch from the guide's embedded application, p.9-10; spot-verify against the PDF). Replaces workbook paraphrase CQ: "Within 3 years: cancer treatment/medication, emphysema/chronic bronchitis/COPD, ulcerative colitis, cirrhosis, hepatitis C or liver disease.". Workbook rows: CQ0012 [CURRENT_CARRIER_2026] https://www.fmiagent.com/wp-content/uploads/2026-07-14_American-Amicable_Golden_Solution_Whole_Life_Advisor_Guide_9507_3-26.pdf Guide p.9 / PDF p.8; CR0015 [CURRENT_CARRIER_2026] https://www.fmiagent.com/wp-content/uploads/2026-07-14_American-Amicable_Golden_Solution_Whole_Life_Advisor_Guide_9507_3-26.pdf Guide pp.9,40; CR0018 [CURRENT_CARRIER_2026] https://www.fmiagent.com/wp-content/uploads/2026-07-14_American-Amicable_Golden_Solution_Whole_Life_Advisor_Guide_9507_3-26.pdf Guide pp.9,40. Lead-in 'diagnosed or treated, or hospitalized for' + '(b) or taken medication for'. 'ulcerative colitis' -> CROHNS_COLITIS (canonical code also covers Crohn's disease, which Q8b does NOT name: over-triggers Crohn's to Graded - confirm the diagnosis). 'liver disease' -> LIVER_DISEASE_OTHER + HEPATITIS_B (liver failure is already a Q2 decline).

rules.text: Within the past 3 years have you been medically diagnosed or treated, or hospitalized for: paralysis of two or more extremities or cerebral palsy, multiple sclerosis, seizures, Parkinson's disease or muscular dystrophy?
rules.note: VERIFIED_FROM_CARRIER_GUIDE via WebFetch (question text as returned by WebFetch from the guide's embedded application, p.9-10; spot-verify against the PDF). 'paralysis of two or more extremities' -> PARALYSIS (canonical: paraplegia/quadriplegia/hemiplegia).

products.carrier: Americo Financial Life and Annuity Insurance Company

classes.label: Eagle Guaranteed (guaranteed issue, 3-year graded)
classes.db: 3-year graded death benefit: Year 1: return of premium plus 5%; Year 2: return of premium plus 10%; Year 3: 75% of the face amount; Year 4+: 100% of the face amount (p.5). Accidental death during the graded period: full death benefit payable (p.9).

stateNotes: Eagle Guaranteed (eApp) is available in all states except NY and WA. (p.11). The guide does not describe any paper application, so WA is treated as unavailable - VERIFY.
MT unisex: the note 'In MT use Male rates for Unisex rates.' is printed beneath the Eagle Premier table on p.13; the guide does not say whether it also applies to Eagle Guaranteed - VERIFY.
notes: Underwriting classes: Male/Female (no tobacco distinction) (p.5).

Issue rule (p.12): Eagle Guaranteed will be issued if: • No health questions are answered on the application, OR • Any health questions (except for the smoker question) on the application are answered “yes” OR • Height and weight are outside guidelines.
$40 annual policy fee (non-commissionable) (p.5). No riders available; accidental death benefit provision included during the graded period at no additional cost (pp.5, 9).
Quit Smoking Advantage is not available on Eagle Guaranteed (p.7).
Only annual (rates are annual per $1,000) and Monthly PAC (0.095) modes are published.
v6: removed from live ranking because current product-generation research points to Americo Eagle Select (current generation). Historical rates remain embedded for comparison/audit.

classes.label: Eagle Premier (Nonsmoker / Smoker)
classes.db: Full death benefit day one (p.5). Smoker policies: Quit Smoking Advantage - see notes (face reduces at year 4 unless insured proves 12 months nicotine-free or elects the Smoker Yrs 4+ premium).

stateNotes: Eagle Premier (eApp) is available in all states except NY. (p.11)
Americo Financial Life and Annuity Insurance Company is authorized to do business in the District of Columbia and all states except NY. (p.14)
In MT use Male rates for Unisex rates. (p.13, printed beneath the Eagle Premier table)
Accelerated Benefit Payment Rider: terminal illness life expectancy 12 months or less (24 months or less in IL, MA, and TX) (p.8)
notes: Quit Smoking Advantage (pp.6-7, 13): the Eagle Premier rate chart has three columns per sex: Non-Smoker, 'Smoker Yrs 1-3' and 'Smoker Yrs 4+*'. 'Smoker Yrs 1-3' is identical to Non-Smoker at every age 40-80 (verified programmatically). Smokers are issued a Smoker policy but pay Nonsmoker rates in policy years 1-3: 'Product quotes should be run for Smoker rates. • The policy will be issued as a Smoker, but the Insured will receive Nonsmoker rates.' (p.7).
Rate table americo_eagle_premier__level, tobacco='T' rows = the 'Smoker Yrs 1-3' column = the premium actually charged at issue for a smoker (ages 40-80 only; smokers 81-85 are n/a).

Rate table americo_eagle_premier__smoker_yrs4plus_keep_face = the 'Smoker Yrs 4+*' column. It is NOT the issue premium. Footnote: '*After year 3, the default option is a decrease in the death benefit, which will keep the policy premium level. These premiums apply when the insured continues to smoke and wants to keep the same death benefit amount as in years 1-3.' (p.13). Use it only to illustrate the optional year-4+ premium for an insured who keeps smoking and elects to keep the original face.

Default year-4 outcome for a continuing smoker: premium stays level and the death benefit is reduced (p.7). The guide gives no formula; the p.6 example (Male 65, $10,000, $65.40/mo) shows $5,438.70, which equals face x NonSmoker rate / Smoker Yrs 4+ rate (10,000 x 64.84/119.22 = 5,438.68) to within $0.02 - derived observation, not a published formula. The ADB rider amount also decreases in year 4 to equal the base face.
Quit Smoking Advantage: 'Not available on Eagle Guaranteed'; issue ages 40-80; earliest proof of quitting is after the first policy year (p.7).
p.6 worked example reproduced exactly with the formula above: Male 65 smoker $10,000 -> (64.84*10+40)*0.095 = $65.40/mo yrs 1-3; keep-face option yrs 4+ -> (119.22*10+40)*0.095 = $117.06/mo.

Riders (p.5, pp.8-9): Accidental Death Benefit Rider (Series 2172) included, ADB = face amount; Accelerated Benefit Payment Rider (Series 2146) included at no cost - up to 50% of death benefit, max $20,000, min $1,000, admin fee up to $250; Child and Grandchild Term Rider (Series 2194) optional, units of $1,000, max lesser of $5,000 or base face per child, cost printed as '$2,10 per $1,000, per child annually' (typo in source, presumably $2.10), children 15 days to under 17 at application, coverage to age 25, max 10 children.
Policy fee $40 annual is commissionable (p.5). Policy Series 311/312/313 (p.1).
Only annual (rates are annual per $1,000) and Monthly PAC (0.095) modes are published; semiannual/quarterly factors are not in the guide.

Underwriting: The products are issued on an Accept/Reject basis according to health questions on the application. A Prescription Drug Check and Medical Information Bureau (MIB) review is required. (p.12). Applicants who do not qualify for Eagle Premier are issued Eagle Guaranteed (product americo_eagle_guaranteed, issue ages 50-80).

rules.text: Have You ever been diagnosed, treated, tested positive, or been given medical advice, or prescribed medication by a licensed member of the medical profession for: a. Alzheimer's disease, dementia, memory loss, muscular dystrophy, or ALS (Lou Gehrig's disease)?

Have You ever been diagnosed, treated, tested positive, or been given medical advice, or prescribed medication by a licensed member of the medical profession for: b. Congestive heart failure, defibrillator placement, cardiomyopathy, chronic kidney disease or kidney failure, or received kidney dialysis?

Have You ever been diagnosed, treated, tested positive, or been given medical advice, or prescribed medication by a licensed member of the medical profession for: c. Cirrhosis of the liver, Hepatitis (all forms, excluding recovered Hepatitis A), or liver failure?
rules.note: 'Hepatitis (all forms, excluding recovered Hepatitis A)': canonical HEPATITIS_B is labeled chronic, but Americo's wording covers any history of Hepatitis B (incl. resolved acute). HEPATITIS_OTHER (proposed) covers autoimmune, alcoholic, drug-induced and unrecovered Hepatitis A. LIVER_DISEASE_OTHER (e.g. fatty liver) is not named and is not mapped.

rules.text: Have You ever been diagnosed, treated, tested positive, or been given medical advice, or prescribed medication by a licensed member of the medical profession for: d. Emphysema, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), or any other chronic respiratory or lung problem, excluding allergies or asthma?
rules.note: 'any other chronic respiratory or lung problem' is open-ended: CHRONIC_BRONCHITIS, PULMONARY_FIBROSIS, CYSTIC_FIBROSIS, SARCOIDOSIS, RESPIRATORY_FAILURE and PULMONARY_HYPERTENSION mapped as chronic lung/respiratory problems. ASTHMA is explicitly excluded. SLEEP_APNEA and TUBERCULOSIS are NOT mapped (Americo treatment unconfirmed - see open_issues). Current/6-month oxygen use is Q10(f).

rules.text: Have You ever been diagnosed, treated, tested positive, or been given medical advice, or prescribed medication by a licensed member of the medical profession for: e. Metastatic cancer (cancer that has spread to other parts of the body)?

Have You ever been diagnosed, treated, tested positive, or been given medical advice, or prescribed medication by a licensed member of the medical profession for: f. Two or more occurrences of cancer of any kind or a reoccurrence of a previous cancer?
rules.note: Matches canonical CANCER_RECURRENT exactly. 'of any kind' as printed includes skin cancers; the interview should count basal/squamous occurrences too if Americo applies the literal wording (unconfirmed).

rules.text: Have You ever been diagnosed, treated, tested positive, or been given medical advice, or prescribed medication by a licensed member of the medical profession for: g. AIDS, ARC, or HIV?
rules.note: California worksheet 13-178-10-CA (10/18) asks HIV/AIDS as a separate question 5 ('Have You ever been diagnosed, treated, or prescribed medication by a licensed member of the medical profession for AIDS or ARC...') and renumbers the rest to Q4-Q12; same outcome.

rules.text: In the past 24 months, have You been diagnosed, treated, tested positive, or been given medical advice by a licensed member of the medical profession for: a. Internal cancer, brain tumor, or malignant melanoma (excluding basal cell skin cancer)?
rules.note: Only basal cell skin cancer is expressly excluded; squamous cell skin cancer is not internal cancer and is not mapped (SKIN_CANCER_BASAL excluded). BRAIN_TUMOR (benign) included because the question names 'brain tumor' without qualification.

rules.text: In the past 24 months, have You been diagnosed, treated, tested positive, or been given medical advice by a licensed member of the medical profession for: b. Complications of diabetes, including amputation, retinopathy (eye disease), nephropathy (kidney disease), neuropathy, insulin shock, or diabetic coma?
rules.note: 'including' is open-ended: DIABETIC_ULCERS added as a diabetic complication. Diabetes itself (pills or insulin) without complications is not asked. Canonical AMPUTATION_DISEASE also covers vascular (non-diabetic) amputation - slight over-trigger. Because the basis is 'any' and treatment counts, a complication that is still being treated (treated_months_ago=0) triggers regardless of when it was diagnosed.

rules.text: In the past 24 months, have You been diagnosed, treated, tested positive, received medical advice, counseling, or been prescribed medication by a licensed member of the medical profession for drug or alcohol abuse/dependency or addiction?

Within the last 12 months, have You been advised, by a licensed member of the medical profession, to have tests, surgery or hospitalization (except for those related to HIV or AIDS), which have not been completed, or are You waiting for a medical diagnosis or results of medical tests or procedures which have not been received?
rules.note: Tests/surgery/hospitalization related to HIV or AIDS are excluded by the question (HIV itself is Q4(g)).

rules.text: In the past 12 months, have You been diagnosed, treated, tested positive, been given medical advice or prescribed medication by a licensed member of the medical profession for: a. Angioplasty (balloon procedure), stent placement, or heart bypass surgery?
rules.note: HEART_SURGERY also covers valve surgery, which Q8(b) 'heart valve disease' covers anyway.

rules.text: In the past 12 months, have You been diagnosed, treated, tested positive, been given medical advice or prescribed medication by a licensed member of the medical profession for: b. Stroke; heart attack, heart valve disease, coronary disease, angina (chest pain), or heart disorder (excluding hypertension)?
rules.note: Basis 'any': diagnosed, treated, given medical advice or prescribed medication in the past 12 months - so ongoing medication for any heart disorder (e.g. AFib on an anticoagulant, CAD on nitrates) triggers. 'heart disorder (excluding hypertension)' mapped to all cardiac codes except HYPERTENSION, HIGH_CHOLESTEROL, PERIPHERAL_VASCULAR_DISEASE, ANEURYSM, BLOOD_CLOTS. TIA is NOT named (only 'Stroke') and is not mapped - see open_issues.

rules.text: Have You received advice from a licensed member of the medical profession to have, are You waiting for, or have You ever received, an organ or tissue transplant?
rules.note: 'tissue transplant' is broader than canonical ORGAN_TRANSPLANT (organ/bone-marrow/stem-cell); e.g. corneal or skin grafts are literally covered - interview should flag ORGAN_TRANSPLANT for any organ or tissue transplant for this carrier.

rules.text: Are You now or within the past 6 months have you been: a. Hospitalized for 48 hours or more, bedridden or confined to or living in a nursing facility or correctional facility?
rules.note: 'now or within the past 6 months' -> within 6 months, basis any (current = treated_months_ago 0 also matches). HOSPITAL_STAY_48H (proposed) = an inpatient stay of 48 hours or more. Canonical INCARCERATED also covers probation/parole, which the question does not name (it asks only about confinement in a correctional facility) - interview should flag it only for confinement.

rules.text: Are You now or within the past 6 months have you been: b. Receiving or been advised by a member of the medical profession to receive hospice care?
Are You now or within the past 6 months have you been: c. Receiving home health care for a chronic or debilitating condition?

Are You now or within the past 6 months have you been: d. Receiving assistance with activities of daily living, including eating, bathing, toileting, or dressing due to a chronic or debilitating condition?

Are You now or within the past 6 months have you been: e. Confined to a wheelchair or using a walker for assistance (except in the case of a temporary condition immediately following injury or medical treatment) not to exceed 3 months' time?
rules.note: Temporary use (not over 3 months) right after an injury or medical treatment is excluded. Canonical WALKER_CANE also includes canes, which the question does not name - interview should flag it only for a walker for this carrier.

rules.text: Are You now or within the past 6 months have you been: f. Using oxygen to assist in breathing?
rules.note: CPAP for sleep apnea is not oxygen (canonical OXYGEN excludes CPAP).

rules.text: Have You been diagnosed with a terminal illness that is expected to result in death within 24 months?
rules.note: Americo threshold is 24 months, matching the outer bound of canonical TERMINAL_ILLNESS.

rules.text: The primary insured has ever been diagnosed, treated, tested positive for, or been given any medical advice by a member of the medical profession for AIDS or HIV, Bipolar disorder, Schizophrenia, Alzheimer’s, Dementia, or other progressive neurologic disorder?

rules.text: Within the last five (5) years, the primary insured has been diagnosed with, hospitalized, treated by a licensed medical profession for Cancer (except basal/squamous cell of the skin), Stroke, Heart Attack, Diabetes (requiring insulin), Chronic Kidney or Liver Disease, or in the past six (6) months has the primary insured undergone diagnostic testing or been advised of the need for diagnostic testing that has not been completed for any of the conditions listed above?

rules.text: Are you currently, or within the past 6 months have you been: hospitalized, bedridden, used oxygen to assist in breathing, confined to a wheelchair, nursing home, hospice, received home health care or been on dialysis?
rules.note: Routing: 'If any answers to questions 3-12 are "YES," the Proposed Insured is not eligible for coverage.' 'currently, or within the past 6 months' -> treated_months_ago <= 6 (0 = current).

rules.text: Are you: a) A resident in, or have you been advised to move into, a nursing home or skilled nursing facility?
rules.note: Verbatim from ICC19 770697 US 07/19 (two identical third-party copies). Question numbering matches the carrier's 10/24 Medical Reference Guide medication chart references. 'Advised to move into' must also be captured as NURSING_FACILITY current.

rules.text: Are you: b) Receiving, or have you been advised to receive, skilled nursing care, hospice care, or home healthcare?
rules.note: Skilled nursing care can be given at home or in a facility; mapped to HOME_HEALTH_CARE and NURSING_FACILITY. 'Advised to receive' counts as current.

rules.text: Are you: c) A patient in a hospital or psychiatric facility, or confined to a correctional facility?
rules.note: INCARCERATED canonical label also covers probation/parole, which this question does not ask about; only current confinement triggers.

rules.text: Are you: d) Using a wheelchair or electric scooter due to an ongoing diagnosed illness, medical condition, or disease?
rules.note: Guide (10/24) 'Wheelchair or electric scooter use' includes injury or disability resulting in permanent and ongoing use.

rules.text: Are you: e) Requiring help (from anyone) with administering or taking your medications, or with bathing, dressing, eating, or toileting?
rules.note: Help taking medications counts as ADL_ASSIST for this carrier. BEDRIDDEN included because a bed-confined applicant requires help with these activities.

rules.text: Within the past year (12 months), have you been advised to: a) Use, or have you used, oxygen equipment to assist with breathing (excluding use for sleep apnea)?
Within the past year (12 months), have you been advised to: b) Have, or have you had, kidney dialysis?

Within the past year (12 months), have you been advised to: c) Have surgery, a medical procedure, hospitalization, or have you been referred for a check up or consultation with a doctor or medical specialist, which has not yet been started, completed, or for which results are not known?
rules.note: Includes pending referrals/consultations with a specialist, which the interview must capture as PENDING_TESTS.

rules.text: Within the past year (12 months), have you been advised to: d) Have a diagnostic test, or have you been referred to get a lab test, which has not yet been started, completed, or for which results are not known (excluding tests related to the Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV))?
rules.note: Pending HIV-related tests are excluded.

rules.text: Within the past year (12 months), have you consulted a physician for, been diagnosed with, or received or been advised to receive treatment or medication for, unexplained weight loss greater than 10 pounds?
rules.note: Proposed code UNEXPLAINED_WEIGHT_LOSS (same code as moo_living_promise).

rules.text: Have you ever received, or been advised to receive, an organ or bone marrow transplant, or had an amputation that you were advised was due to complications of diabetes?
rules.note: AMPUTATION_DISEASE canonical label also covers vascular-disease amputations; the question names diabetes only. The medication chart cites '4b(FL)' for HIV drugs, i.e. the Florida form adds an HIV item as Q4(b) (Florida form not obtained).

rules.text: Have you ever been diagnosed with, or received or been advised to receive treatment or medication for: a) Cardiomyopathy, Congestive Heart Failure (CHF), Pulmonary Hypertension, or any other type of heart failure or heart muscle disease?
Have you ever been diagnosed with, or received or been advised to receive treatment or medication for: b) Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS), or a terminal illness or end-stage disease?
rules.note: Application defines terminal illness as 'an illness that would reasonably be expected to cause death within 12 months'. END_STAGE_DISEASE is a proposed code (guide 10/24 definition).

rules.text: Have you ever been diagnosed with, or received or been advised to receive treatment or medication for: c) Alzheimer's disease, dementia, or memory loss?
rules.note: Guide: memory loss includes mild cognitive impairment (MCI).

rules.text: Have you ever been diagnosed with, or received or been advised to receive treatment or medication for: d) Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome (AIDS), AIDS Related Complex (ARC), or tested positive for HIV?
rules.note: Canonical HIV_AIDS label also includes other immune deficiency disorders; this question asks only about AIDS/ARC/HIV.

rules.text: Have you ever been diagnosed with more than one occurrence of the same or different type of cancer, or do you currently have cancer (the term 'cancer' excludes basal cell skin cancer)?
rules.note: Squamous cell skin cancer is NOT excluded by the wording (only basal cell); canonical SKIN_CANCER_BASAL lumps basal and squamous.

rules.text: Have you ever been diagnosed with diabetes and have also been diagnosed with, or advised to receive treatment for: a) Retinopathy (problems with your eyesight)? b) Nephropathy (kidney disease or kidney damage)? c) Peripheral Neuropathy (nerve damage or numbness)?
rules.note: Guide 10/24: Nephropathy/Diabetic, Peripheral Neuropathy/Diabetic, Retinopathy/Diabetic -> 'Anytime – Basic Death Benefit'.

rules.text: Within the past 2 years (24 months), have you been hospitalized for 48 hours or more that you were advised was due to diabetes?
rules.note: Proposed code DIABETES_HOSPITALIZATION_48H (diabetes-caused stay of 48h+; diagnosed_months_ago = discharge date).

rules.text: Within the past 2 years (24 months), have you been diagnosed with, or received or been advised to receive treatment for: a) Alcohol or drug abuse, or have you used illegal drugs?
rules.note: Guide 10/24 'Illegal Drugs': drugs without a prescription or not legal in the applicant's state of residence -> within 2 years Basic.

rules.text: Within the past 2 years (24 months), have you been diagnosed with, or received or been advised to receive treatment for: b) An aneurysm, or have you ever been diagnosed with an aneurysm that has not yet been repaired?
rules.note: ANEURYSM_UNREPAIRED is a proposed code (aneurysm not repaired or removed, any duration).

rules.text: Within the past 2 years (24 months), have you been diagnosed with, or received or been advised to receive treatment for: c) A brain tumor, or have you ever been diagnosed with a brain tumor that has not yet been treated or is being monitored or observed?
rules.note: BRAIN_TUMOR_UNTREATED is a proposed code (brain tumor not yet treated/removed or under monitoring/observation). Malignant brain tumors also hit Q6/Q12 as CANCER.

rules.text: Within the past year (12 months), have you been diagnosed with having: a) A heart attack, stroke, or Transient Ischemic Attack (TIA/mini-stroke)?
rules.note: Basis 'diagnosed' = date of the event; for repeat events the interview must use the MOST RECENT event date. Ongoing post-event medication (e.g., Plavix) does not by itself answer this question 'yes'.

rules.text: Within the past year (12 months), have you been diagnosed with having: b) Angina, or have you taken medication for angina?
rules.note: Taking angina medication (e.g., nitroglycerin, Ranexa) within 12 months answers yes.

rules.text: Within the past year (12 months), have you been advised to have, or have you had, a pacemaker or defibrillator implant, cardioversion treatment, or any other type of heart or circulatory procedure?
rules.note: Basis 'diagnosed' = procedure/implant date (guide: 'Implant within 1 yr'). A procedure advised but not yet done also triggers Q2(c) (DECLINE). CARDIOVERSION and CIRCULATORY_SURGERY are proposed codes.

rules.text: Within the past 3 years (36 months), have you been diagnosed with cancer, or received or been advised to receive chemotherapy, radiation, or any other type of treatment for cancer (the term 'cancer' excludes basal cell skin cancer)?
rules.note: The 10/24 medication chart treats hormonal cancer drugs (Arimidex, Femara, tamoxifen, etc.) STARTED more than 3 years ago as Preferred, so ongoing hormonal therapy alone is not treated as 'treatment within 3 years' by the carrier (see open_issues).

rules.text: Have you ever been diagnosed with, or received or been advised to receive treatment or medication for: a) Parkinson's disease or Systemic Lupus (SLE)?
rules.note: Guide: Parkinson's is Standard only if able to perform all ADLs, otherwise No Coverage (ADL help also triggers Q1(e)).

rules.text: Have you ever been diagnosed with, or received or been advised to receive treatment or medication for: b) Hepatitis B or C, cirrhosis of the liver, or any other type of liver disease or condition?

Have you ever been diagnosed with, or received or been advised to receive treatment or medication for: c) Chronic kidney disease, chronic renal insufficiency, or any other type of kidney disease or condition (excluding kidney stones)?
rules.note: Kidney stones excluded. Guide: 'Kidney Disease/Renal Insufficiency ... Also called renal disease, renal insufficiency or kidney/renal failure' -> Standard. Dialysis within 12 months is Q2(b) DECLINE; older dialysis falls here. Diabetic nephropathy is Q7 (Basic).

rules.text: Have you ever been diagnosed with, or received or been advised to receive treatment or medication for: d) Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD), chronic bronchitis, emphysema, or any other type of chronic lung disease or ongoing respiratory condition (excluding asthma or sleep apnea)?
rules.note: Asthma and sleep apnea excluded by the wording. TUBERCULOSIS not mapped (infectious, not necessarily chronic) - interview should treat chronic/active TB as an 'ongoing respiratory condition'.

rules.text: Within the past 2 years (24 months), have you been diagnosed with having: a) A heart attack, stroke, or Transient Ischemic Attack (TIA/mini-stroke)?
rules.note: See Q10(a) note on event dates.

rules.text: Within the past 2 years (24 months), have you been diagnosed with having: b) Angina, or have you taken medication for angina?

Within the past 2 years (24 months), have you been advised to have, or have you had, a pacemaker or defibrillator implant, cardioversion treatment, or any other type of heart or circulatory procedure?
rules.note: See Q11 note.

products.carrier: Greek Catholic Union of the U.S.A. (GCU) - fraternal

classes.label: Preferred
classes.db: Level: full face amount (no graded period stated for Preferred/Standard).

classes.label: Standard
classes.db: Level: full face amount (no graded period stated for Preferred/Standard).

classes.label: Modified
classes.db: "Modified: provides a graded death benefit equal to a return of premium plus 10% during the first three certificate years and $1,000 per unit beginning in the fourth certificate year. During the first three certificate years, only upon accidental death will the ultimate (full) death benefit be paid." (rate book, via WebFetch)

stateNotes: "Product features, riders and availability may vary by state." (UW guide) - state list not captured; workbook State_Scope 'See current GCU state availability'.
notes: Issue ages 45-85 Age Last Birthday (UW guide p.1 via WebFetch); workbook rate rows 45-85 for all classes.
Face: Preferred $5,000-$35,000; Standard $5,000-$25,000; Modified $5,000-$15,000 (UW guide p.1 via WebFetch).
Six risk classes: Preferred, Standard, Modified, each Tobacco / Non-Tobacco (UW guide).

Policy fee $40/year ("included in base policy premium (commissionable in year one)" - UW guide; rate book: rates are per $1,000 'Plus $40 Policy Fee'). Modal factors semi-annual .52, quarterly .26, monthly EFT .09 (rate book). Workbook: $40 fee, monthly .09 - agrees.

classes.db: Level death benefit from date of issue

classes.db: Level death benefit from date of issue

classes.label: SIMPL Modified
classes.db: First 3 policy years: accidental death 100% of face; non-accidental death = refund of all premiums paid to date plus 10% compounded. 4th policy year 100%; 5th policy year 105%; 6th policy year and beyond 110%.

stateNotes: Rate book has no state-specific rates or availability list; back cover (p.63): 'Not all products are available in all states. For information about your state, please contact Liberty Bankers at 919-788-8097.'
notes: Modal factors (pp.5-8,25-28,45-48 'PREMIUM FACTORS FOR ALL FINAL EXPENSE PLANS'): Annual (1st year) x 0.80; Annual (2nd year & thereafter) x 1.00; Semi-Annual x 0.51; Quarterly x 0.265; Monthly (PAC or SS) x 0.0925; 'Round all fractions to the nearest cent.'

Policy fee $50.00 annual, same for all three classes ('Add $50.00 Annual Policy Fee' on every rate page); the fee is multiplied by the modal factor (verified: book monthly quick quotes = round((rate*face/1000 + 50) * 0.0925, 2), 7,345 of 7,345 printed cells).
Minimum modal premium $15 (p.4) for every mode. Book's Modified $1,000-face monthly quick quotes (p.49-52) are below $15 (e.g. $8.20) - engine should enforce the $15 minimum.
Issue ages for Preferred/Standard read '18 to 80 Male & Female (see Direct Express limitations**)' - the ** footnote is not printed anywhere in the book.
Age basis (ANB vs ALB) not stated in the rate book.
Face increment not stated in the rate book.
Modified issue ages 40-80 only: an applicant under 40 who routes to Modified has no available SIMPL class.
Rate book also prints cash values (Yr10/Yr20/Age 65; Modified: CV and reduced paid-up Yr10/Yr20) - not extracted.

rules.text: Have you, the Proposed Insured, ever been diagnosed, treated, tested positive for, or been given medical advice by a member of the medical profession for: a. Congestive heart failure (CHF), cardiomyopathy, memory loss, Alzheimer's, senile dementia, dementia, heart defibrillator implant, two or more instances of internal cancer(s), or terminal illness ("terminal illness" means a disease or illness that is expected to result in death within 24 months)?
rules.note: Verbatim from Ordinary Life Agent Guide LBIG-0523-POLAG1 p.4 (embedded ICC22-TAPP-LBL questions); fetched twice with identical wording. Terminal illness here = expected death within 24 months.

rules.text: Have you, the Proposed Insured, ever been diagnosed, treated, tested positive for, or been given medical advice by a member of the medical profession for: b. Organ transplant (other than corneal), bone marrow transplant, stem cell treatment, kidney failure or dialysis, muscular dystrophy, mental incapacity, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) or Lou Gehrig's disease, Downs's syndrome, cystic fibrosis, pulmonary fibrosis, or Huntington's disease?
rules.note: Verbatim from Ordinary Life Agent Guide LBIG-0523-POLAG1 p.4 (embedded ICC22-TAPP-LBL questions); fetched twice with identical wording. Corneal transplant excluded. Stem cell treatment and bone marrow transplant -> ORGAN_TRANSPLANT (label includes bone-marrow/stem-cell). 'Mental incapacity' -> MEMORY_LOSS (canonical label includes mental incapacity).

rules.text: Have you, the Proposed Insured, ever been diagnosed, treated, tested positive for, or been given medical advice by a member of the medical profession for: c. Diabetes at age 9 or younger?
rules.note: Verbatim from Ordinary Life Agent Guide LBIG-0523-POLAG1 p.4 (embedded ICC22-TAPP-LBL questions); fetched twice with identical wording.

rules.text: Have you, the Proposed Insured, ever been diagnosed, treated, tested positive for, or been given medical advice by a member of the medical profession for: d. Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome (AIDS), AIDS Related Complex, tested positive for human immunodeficiency viruses (HIV), or any other disorder of the immune system?
rules.note: Verbatim from Ordinary Life Agent Guide LBIG-0523-POLAG1 p.4 (embedded ICC22-TAPP-LBL questions); fetched twice with identical wording. 'Any other disorder of the immune system' is broad; canonical HIV_AIDS covers 'immune deficiency disorder'. Autoimmune diseases are not mapped here because Q5e separately routes SLE to MWL (see open_issues).

rules.text: Have you, by a member of the medical profession, within the prior 2 years, been diagnosed with, or received, or been advised to receive treatment or medication for uncontrolled diabetes, uncontrolled high blood pressure, a diabetic coma or insulin shock, amputation due to diabetic complications, schizophrenia, alcohol / drug abuse, illegal use of drugs, or dependency on prescription medication?
rules.note: Verbatim from Ordinary Life Agent Guide LBIG-0523-POLAG1 p.4 (embedded ICC22-TAPP-LBL questions); fetched twice with identical wording. HYPERTENSION_UNCONTROLLED is a proposed code (already proposed in liberty_bankers_simpl/uw.json). Prescription-drug dependency -> DRUG_ABUSE. AMPUTATION_DISEASE label also covers vascular amputations; question names diabetic complications only.

rules.text: Within the last year, have you been confined to a hospital for more than 5 days total, been advised by a member of the medical profession to have surgery or hospitalization which you are still awaiting, used oxygen due to a medical condition, been unable to care for yourself or been bedridden at home or in a nursing home, hospice, long-term care, or assisted living facility?
rules.note: Verbatim from Ordinary Life Agent Guide LBIG-0523-POLAG1 p.4 (embedded ICC22-TAPP-LBL questions); fetched twice with identical wording. HOSPITAL_DAYS (proposed, total inpatient days; >5 => count_gte 6). 'Unable to care for yourself' -> ADL_ASSIST. Nursing home / hospice / LTC / assisted-living confinement within the last year mapped to NURSING_FACILITY/HOSPICE (the clause can be read as only 'bedridden ... in' those settings; conservative reading used). Home health care is not named and is not mapped.

rules.text: Within the past 3 years have you, the Proposed Insured, been diagnosed, treated, tested positive for, or been given medical advice by a member of the medical profession for lymphoma, leukemia or any form of cancer or received or been advised to receive chemotherapy or radiation for cancer (the term "cancer" includes melanoma, but excludes basal cell skin cancer)?
rules.note: Verbatim from Ordinary Life Agent Guide LBIG-0523-POLAG1 p.4 (embedded ICC22-TAPP-LBL questions); fetched twice with identical wording. Squamous cell skin cancer is not excluded by the wording.

rules.text: Within the past 2 years have you, the Proposed Insured, been diagnosed, treated, tested positive for, or been given medical advice by a member of the medical profession for: a. Angina (chest pain), any type of heart or circulatory surgery or disease, heart valve disorder, heart attack, or received a pacemaker or stent?
rules.note: Verbatim from Ordinary Life Agent Guide LBIG-0523-POLAG1 p.4 (embedded ICC22-TAPP-LBL questions); fetched twice with identical wording. 'Any type of heart or circulatory ... disease' could literally include AFib/irregular heartbeat and PVD/PAD within 2 years, but Part 3 Q7a names those specifically (ever -> Standard); they are NOT mapped here (see open_issues). CIRCULATORY_SURGERY is a proposed code.

rules.text: Within the past 2 years have you, the Proposed Insured, been diagnosed, treated, tested positive for, or been given medical advice by a member of the medical profession for: b. Stroke (excluding Transient Ischemic Attack / TIA / mini-stroke) or paralysis?
rules.note: Verbatim from Ordinary Life Agent Guide LBIG-0523-POLAG1 p.4 (embedded ICC22-TAPP-LBL questions); fetched twice with identical wording. TIA excluded here (TIA is Part 3 Q8).

rules.text: Within the past 2 years have you, the Proposed Insured, been diagnosed, treated, tested positive for, or been given medical advice by a member of the medical profession for: c. Aneurysm, brain tumor, or sickle cell anemia?
rules.note: Verbatim from Ordinary Life Agent Guide LBIG-0523-POLAG1 p.4 (embedded ICC22-TAPP-LBL questions); fetched twice with identical wording.

rules.text: Within the past 2 years have you, the Proposed Insured, been diagnosed, treated, tested positive for, or been given medical advice by a member of the medical profession for: d. Complications of diabetes such as nephropathy (kidney), neuropathy (nerve, circulatory), retinopathy (eye)?
rules.note: Verbatim from Ordinary Life Agent Guide LBIG-0523-POLAG1 p.4 (embedded ICC22-TAPP-LBL questions); fetched twice with identical wording. 'neuropathy (nerve, circulatory)' -> DIABETIC_ULCERS (poor circulation from diabetes) included.

rules.text: Within the past 2 years have you, the Proposed Insured, been diagnosed, treated, tested positive for, or been given medical advice by a member of the medical profession for: e. Chronic hepatitis, Hepatitis C, cirrhosis of the liver, chronic pancreatitis, kidney disease or Systemic Lupus (SLE)?
rules.note: Verbatim from Ordinary Life Agent Guide LBIG-0523-POLAG1 p.4 (embedded ICC22-TAPP-LBL questions); fetched twice with identical wording. 'Chronic hepatitis' -> HEPATITIS_B (chronic) + HEPATITIS_C; other chronic hepatitis types have no canonical code (americo proposed HEPATITIS_OTHER).

rules.text: Within the past 2 years have you, the Proposed Insured, been diagnosed, treated, tested positive for, or been given medical advice by a member of the medical profession for: f. Multiple sclerosis, Parkinson's disease, or required the use of a walker, wheelchair, or electric scooter due to chronic illness or disease?
rules.note: Verbatim from Ordinary Life Agent Guide LBIG-0523-POLAG1 p.4 (embedded ICC22-TAPP-LBL questions); fetched twice with identical wording. Question names a walker, not a cane; canonical WALKER_CANE lumps both.

rules.text: In the last two years, have you plead guilty to or been convicted of a felony or misdemeanor or do you have such a charge currently pending against you?
rules.note: Verbatim from Ordinary Life Agent Guide LBIG-0523-POLAG1 p.4 (embedded ICC22-TAPP-LBL questions); fetched twice with identical wording. DUI included because a DUI conviction is a misdemeanor or felony conviction.

rules.text: Have you, the Proposed Insured, by a member of the medical profession, ever been diagnosed with, or received, or been advised to receive treatment or medication for: a. Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD), chronic bronchitis, emphysema, irregular heartbeat, atrial fibrillation, peripheral vascular disease or peripheral artery disease?

uw.routingText: p.4: Part 1 (Q1a-Q3) - 'If the applicant answers "Yes" to any question in Part 1, STOP with the application.' -> DECLINE. 'If all "No" answers in Part 1, Proposed Insured should answer Part 2.' Part 2 (Q4-Q6) - 'If any "Yes" answer(s) in Part 2, Proposed Insured may qualify for MWL (check state availability), answer Part 3.' -> MODIFIED (Modified Whole Life). Part 3 (Q7a-Q8) - 'If all "No" answers in Part 3, Proposed Insured may qualify for SIMPL Preferred.' -> any Part 3 Yes = SIMPL STANDARD (inferred), all No = PREFERRED. Then build chart p.5 (class = best class whose max >= weight; under min or over MWL max -> DECLINE) and MIB + Rx Check ('Guideline as to whether the medication is an autodecline by product tier (preferred, standard, or modified.)', p.8). MWL is subject to state availability.

classes.label: Graded Benefit
classes.db: This policy contains a graded benefit meaning that for death due to natural causes (any cause other than accidental) during the first two years, the beneficiary will receive all premiums paid plus 10 percent. After the two years, the full benefit is paid for death due to all causes. Full death benefits will be paid, in all years, if death results from an accidental bodily injury. (p.2)

stateNotes: WA: Level face amounts $5,000 - $40,000; Graded face amounts $5,000 - $20,000 (p.2)
Graded Benefit Plan not available in AR, MT, NC (p.2)
NOTE: In MT only, Unisex rates apply. The male rates listed apply to Unisex rates in MT. (p.3, Level Benefit table)
United of Omaha does not conduct business in New York (p.8)
Accelerated Death Benefit rider is the Terminal Illness or Chronic Illness Rider in FL and the Terminal Illness Rider in CT (p.2)
Suicide exclusion: two years from contestability date; one year in ND (p.5)
notes: Underwriting classes: Level = Standard Tobacco/Nontobacco; Graded = Standard (no tobacco distinction) (p.2).
Underwriting requirements (both plans): MIB, pharmaceutical check, random phone interviews (p.2); telephone interview approx. 20 minutes, recorded (p.7).

Combined maximum limits (p.5): Living Promise Level - no more than $40,000 of Living Promise Level Benefit coverage; no more than $50,000 of all simplified issue coverage with United of Omaha. Living Promise Graded - no more than $20,000 of Living Promise Graded Benefit coverage; no more than $25,000 of all graded benefit coverage with United of Omaha.

Level Benefit Plan only: Accelerated Death Benefit for Terminal Illness or Nursing Home Confinement Rider included; optional Accidental Death Benefit Rider (benefit = face amount) (p.2). ADB rider premiums by issue age 45-85 are in rates.json table moo_living_promise__adb_rider; the rider table is printed under the page heading 'Annual Premiums per $1,000 of Coverage' (p.4) but has no unit label of its own - treat as annual per $1,000 of rider coverage, VERIFY.

Annual policy fee: $36 Level (p.3 footnote), $12 Graded (p.4 footnote). The guide does not print a worked premium example; applying the modal factor to (rates + fee) is the standard reading - VERIFY against a carrier quote.
Premium modes (p.4): Annual (1.00), Semiannual (.52), Quarterly (.275), Monthly BSP (.089).
Age basis (ALB/ANB) is not stated anywhere in guide 461606.
Conditional receipt coverage max: $40,000 Level / $20,000 Graded (p.7).

rules.text: Has the Proposed Insured ever been diagnosed by a member of the medical profession or been tested positive for Human Immunodeficiency Virus (AIDS Virus) or Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome (AIDS)?
rules.note: Q1 sits under the Part One header, but the Part One instruction names only 'QUESTIONS 2-5' and no consequence for a Q1 'yes' is printed (same in the OCI health-question guide). Modeled DECLINE because (1) Mutual of Omaha's Rx exclusion list 170121_0823 says proposed insureds currently taking HIV drugs (Atripla, Isentress, Stribild, etc.) 'are not eligible for Living Promise coverage' and (2) HIV/AIDS was a Part One (decline) item on the pre-8/2023 application. Q1 is the state-variable question: the Florida form T210LFL23A words it 'Has the Proposed Insured ever tested positive for exposure to the HIV infection or been diagnosed by a licensed medical professional as having Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome (AIDS) or AIDS Related Complex (ARC) caused by the HIV infection or other sickness or condition derived from such infection?'

rules.text: Is the Proposed Insured currently: (a) bedridden or confined to any hospital, nursing home, long-term care facility or skilled nursing facility; or receiving or been advised by a member of the medical profession to receive care in a nursing home, hospice care, or home health care?
rules.note: 'Advised ... to receive care in a nursing home ... or home health care' also triggers; canonical NURSING_FACILITY/HOME_HEALTH_CARE describe receiving care, so the interview must also flag them current when care has been advised but not started (HOSPICE label already includes 'advised').

rules.text: Is the Proposed Insured currently: (b) requiring assistance with activities of daily living such as taking medications, bathing, dressing, eating, toileting, getting in and out of a chair or bed, or control of bowel or bladder problems?
rules.note: MoO's ADL list includes 'taking medications', which the canonical ADL_ASSIST label does not name; interview should treat needing help taking medications as ADL_ASSIST for this carrier.

rules.text: Is the Proposed Insured currently: (c) requiring any of the following (other than for fractures, bone or joint surgery, including replacement): wheelchair, electric scooter, advised by a member of the medical profession to use oxygen equipment to assist breathing (excluding use for sleep apnea) or defibrillator?
rules.note: Wheelchair/scooter use solely for fractures or bone/joint surgery (incl. replacement) is excluded by the question; canonical WHEELCHAIR is 'due to chronic illness or disease', which matches. 'Defibrillator' = implanted ICD currently in place.

rules.text: Has the Proposed Insured ever (i) been diagnosed with, (ii) received treatment for, or (iii) been advised by a member of the medical profession to seek treatment for: (a) Alzheimer's Disease, Dementia, Huntington's Disease, Sickle Cell Anemia, Myelodysplastic Syndrome (MDS), Lou Gehrig's Disease (ALS), Hydrocephalus, Muscular Dystrophy, Quadriplegia, Paraplegia, Down Syndrome, Intellectual Developmental Disorder, Congestive Heart Failure, Cirrhosis, Metastatic Cancer or recurrent Cancer of the same type?
rules.note: MYELODYSPLASTIC_SYNDROME and HYDROCEPHALUS are proposed codes (canonical BLOOD_DISORDER also covers hemophilia/aplastic anemia, which MoO does not list here). If the interview only captures MDS as BLOOD_DISORDER this rule will miss it. Quadriplegia/Paraplegia mapped to PARALYSIS, whose canonical label also includes hemiplegia (not named by MoO) - over-triggers for hemiplegia only. 'Intellectual Developmental Disorder' mapped to DOWN_SYNDROME (canonical label covers intellectual/developmental disability). 'recurrent Cancer of the same type' mapped to CANCER_RECURRENT, whose canonical label also covers two different cancers - over-triggers when the second cancer is a different type.

rules.text: Has the Proposed Insured ever (i) been diagnosed with, (ii) received treatment for, or (iii) been advised by a member of the medical profession to seek treatment for: (b) insulin shock, diabetic coma, amputation due to diabetic complications, End Stage Renal Disease or requiring dialysis?
rules.note: End Stage Renal Disease mapped to KIDNEY_FAILURE. Canonical AMPUTATION_DISEASE also covers amputation from vascular disease; MoO names only amputation due to diabetic complications.

rules.text: Has the Proposed Insured ever (i) been diagnosed with, (ii) received treatment for, or (iii) been advised by a member of the medical profession to seek treatment for: (c) an organ or bone marrow transplant?

Has the Proposed Insured ever (i) been diagnosed with, (ii) received treatment for, or (iii) been advised by a member of the medical profession to seek treatment for: (d) a terminal medical condition that is expected to result in death within the next twelve (12) months?
rules.note: MoO threshold is life expectancy of 12 months or less; canonical TERMINAL_ILLNESS spans 12-24 months, so a 13-24 month prognosis over-triggers this rule.

rules.text: In the past 12 months, has the Proposed Insured been: (a) advised by a member of the medical profession to have a surgical operation, diagnostic testing (other than for routine screening purposes or for those related to HIV/AIDS), treatment, hospitalization, or other procedure which has not been done or for which results are not known?
rules.note: Routine screening and HIV/AIDS-related testing are excluded by the question.

rules.text: In the past 12 months, has the Proposed Insured been: (b) diagnosed by a member of the medical profession as having heart disease or heart surgery of any kind?
rules.note: Literal reading: diagnosis of heart disease (or a heart surgery/procedure) within the past 12 months; basis 'diagnosed'. For procedure codes (HEART_SURGERY, ANGIOPLASTY_STENT, PACEMAKER, DEFIBRILLATOR) diagnosed_months_ago must be the date of the MOST RECENT procedure. Hypertension and high cholesterol are not heart disease and are not mapped. Older heart history is handled by Part Two Q8 (2 years -> Graded).

rules.text: In the past 2 years, has the Proposed Insured been diagnosed with, been treated for or advised by a member of the medical profession to receive treatment for any form of cancer (except basal or squamous cell skin cancer)?

rules.ref: Q6(a) (printed after the tobacco question, before the Part Two header)
rules.text: Has the Proposed Insured ever (i) been diagnosed with, (ii) received treatment for, or (iii) been advised by a member of the medical profession to seek treatment for: (a) Diabetes before age 45?
rules.note: See open_issues: Q6 is printed above the Part Two header but is not one of the decline questions (Part One instruction names only Q2-5). Routed GRADED per the OCI health question guide ('Any "yes" answers to questions 6-11 may qualify for the Mutual of Omaha graded benefit plan') and the closing note (all 'No' -> Level). MoO's 8/2023 producer notice: 'We've lowered the age for diabetes automatic declines to 45. (It was previously 50).' - the previous before-50 diabetes question was a Part Two (Graded) question.

rules.ref: Q6(b) (printed after the tobacco question, before the Part Two header)
rules.text: Has the Proposed Insured ever (i) been diagnosed with, (ii) received treatment for, or (iii) been advised by a member of the medical profession to seek treatment for: (b) Diabetes at any age with complications or history of Retinopathy (eye), Nephropathy (kidney), Neuropathy (nerve), Peripheral Vascular Disease (PVD or PAD), Coronary Artery Disease (CAD) or Stroke?
rules.note: PVD/PAD, CAD and Stroke trigger this question only when the applicant also has diabetes - expressed with the proposed extra predicate 'also_has_any' (see proposed_codes). 'with complications' is open-ended: DIABETIC_ULCERS included as a diabetic complication; DIABETIC_COMA and diabetic amputation are already Part One Q3(b) declines. DIABETES_UNCONTROLLED alone is not a named complication and is not mapped.

rules.ref: Q6(c) (printed after the tobacco question, before the Part Two header)
rules.text: Has the Proposed Insured ever (i) been diagnosed with, (ii) received treatment for, or (iii) been advised by a member of the medical profession to seek treatment for: (c) Hepatitis C?
rules.note: See Q6(a) note on routing.

rules.ref: Q6(d) (printed after the tobacco question, before the Part Two header)
rules.text: Has the Proposed Insured ever (i) been diagnosed with, (ii) received treatment for, or (iii) been advised by a member of the medical profession to seek treatment for: (d) Chronic Lung Disease, including Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD), Chronic Bronchitis, Emphysema, or Sarcoidosis?
rules.note: 'Chronic Lung Disease, including ...' is open-ended; PULMONARY_FIBROSIS, CYSTIC_FIBROSIS and RESPIRATORY_FAILURE (chronic respiratory disorder) added as chronic lung diseases. ASTHMA, SLEEP_APNEA, TUBERCULOSIS and PULMONARY_HYPERTENSION are NOT mapped (not named; carrier treatment unconfirmed). Oxygen use is a Part One Q2(c) decline. See Q6(a) note on routing.

rules.text: In the past 4 years, has the Proposed Insured: (i) been diagnosed with, (ii) received treatment for, or (iii) been advised by a member of the medical profession to seek treatment for: (a) Cancer, Leukemia, or any other internal cancer or Melanoma (except basal or squamous cell skin cancer)?
rules.note: Cancer within 2 years is a Part One Q5 decline; worst-outcome evaluation makes the 25-48 month band Graded.

rules.text: In the past 4 years, has the Proposed Insured: (i) been diagnosed with, (ii) received treatment for, or (iii) been advised by a member of the medical profession to seek treatment for: (b) Chronic Kidney Disease, Systemic Lupus or Scleroderma?

In the past 4 years, has the Proposed Insured: (i) been diagnosed with, (ii) received treatment for, or (iii) been advised by a member of the medical profession to seek treatment for: (c) Bipolar Depression, Schizophrenia, Parkinson's Disease or Multiple Sclerosis?

In the past 2 years, has the Proposed Insured: (i) been diagnosed with, (ii) received treatment for, or (iii) been advised by a member of the medical profession to seek treatment for: (a) Coronary Artery Disease, Heart Attack, Coronary Artery Bypass Surgery, Angioplasty, Cardiomyopathy, irregular heart rhythm, Pacemaker or Valvular Heart Disease with surgical repair or replacement?
rules.note: 'Valvular Heart Disease with surgical repair or replacement' and 'Coronary Artery Bypass Surgery' map to HEART_SURGERY; HEART_VALVE_DISORDER without surgery is not named and is not mapped here. ANGINA included as a manifestation of coronary artery disease. Cardiomyopathy and heart disease diagnosed within 12 months are Part One Q4(b) declines.

rules.text: In the past 2 years, has the Proposed Insured: (i) been diagnosed with, (ii) received treatment for, or (iii) been advised by a member of the medical profession to seek treatment for: (b) Stroke or Transient Ischemic Attack (TIA)?
In the past 2 years, has the Proposed Insured: (a) been convicted of or currently awaiting trial for a felony?
rules.note: FELONY window uses the conviction date. Canonical CHARGES_PENDING is not limited to felonies; the interview should only flag it for pending felony charges for this carrier.

rules.text: In the past 2 years, has the Proposed Insured: (b) been treated for or advised by a member of the medical profession to have treatment for alcohol or drug abuse, convicted of driving under the influence of drugs or alcohol or convicted more than once of reckless driving?
rules.note: RECKLESS_DRIVING is a proposed code (already proposed by transamerica_* products); detail.count = number of reckless-driving convictions in the 2-year lookback.

rules.text: In the past 2 years, has the Proposed Insured: (c) used unlawful drugs in any form (other than marijuana) or abused or misused prescription drugs?
rules.note: Marijuana is excluded (MoO 8/2023 notice: 'Marijuana is no longer considered an "unlawful drug" for the purposes of the application and underwriting').

rules.text: In the past 2 years, has the Proposed Insured been hospitalized by a member of the medical profession for any mental or nervous disorder?

In the past 12 months, has the Proposed Insured been diagnosed or treated by a member of the medical profession for chronic cough, unexplained weight loss greater than 10 pounds, fatigue or unexplained gastrointestinal bleeding?
rules.note: All four are proposed codes (no canonical equivalents). UNEXPLAINED_WEIGHT_LOSS means unexplained loss greater than 10 pounds.

uw.routingText: Part One Q2-Q5 any YES -> DECLINE (app: 'IF THE PROPOSED INSURED ANSWERS “YES” TO QUESTIONS 2-5 IN PART ONE, THAT PERSON IS NOT ELIGIBLE FOR ANY COVERAGE UNDER THIS APPLICATION.'). Q1 (HIV/AIDS) YES -> modeled DECLINE (not named in the Part One instruction; see open_issues). Q6 (diabetes/Hep C/chronic lung) YES -> GRADED. Part Two Q7-Q11 any YES -> GRADED (app: 'IF THE PROPOSED INSURED ANSWERS “YES” TO ANY QUESTION IN PART TWO, THAT PERSON IS ELIGIBLE ONLY FOR THE GRADED BENEFIT PRODUCT.'). All NO -> LEVEL (app: 'NOTE: If the Proposed Insured answers all above questions “No”, that person is eligible for the Level Benefit Product.'). Tobacco question sets the Level tobacco/non-tobacco rate class only (Graded has no tobacco distinction). Graded issue ages 45-80; Graded not available where product.json says so. Final class = worst outcome across these rules, build and Rx.

notes: Plan placement is by application Section 7 medical questions (Parts A/B/C) - see uw.json notes. The question texts are NOT printed in this guide.

Issue ages by premium plan for NV I (age last birthday): Single Premium 20-76 (max varies by sex/nicotine), Ordinary 0-85, 10-Pay 0-75, 20-Pay 0-65, Paid-Up 65 0-55, Paid-Up 85 0-65. NV I nicotine rates start at age 18.
NV II and NV III: issue ages 45-85, premiums level payable to age 121 (whole life only).
Minimum face: Single Premium $2,000; all others $1,000. Minimum premium $10 per month.
Policy fee $35 annually (commissionable).
NV I rate tables for 10 Pay, 20 Pay, Paid-Up 65, Paid-Up 85 and Single Premium are in rates.json (not referenced by plan_classes; plan class NV_I uses Full Pay).

Riders: NV I - Accidental Death (ADR; issue ages 0-60; up to 5x face max $100,000; $1.25 per 1,000 annual), Children's Protection (CPR; $10 per unit annually), Waiver of Premium (WOP; issue ages 15-55). NV II/III - ADR included in first two years at no additional cost; CPR and WOP N/A.
Underwriting classes: Non-Nicotine, Nicotine. Cash value/loans available.
MIB report ordered on every proposed insured; APS may be ordered in certain rare cases.
Policy may be back-dated by written request, not more than six months; back premiums collected with application. Post-dated checks within 30 days accepted.

Third-party applications: As a general rule, on third party applications, any adult insured must sign the application and a statement of insurable interest must be completed by the owner. Exceptions: parent on minor children, adult child on parent(s) (insured parent must sign), spouse (spouse must sign), grandparent on minor grandchildren.
Policy forms 90B-XX, 90E-XX, 90F-XX, 90G-XX.

rules.text: Is the Proposed Insured currently: bedridden, confined to a nursing or correctional facility, receiving hospice or home health care, received or been advised to receive an organ or tissue transplant, or been hospitalized within the last 3 months?
rules.note: Part A header: 'if any question is answered "Yes," the Applicant is not eligible for coverage (Circle any impairments that apply)'. 'confined to a ... correctional facility' mapped to INCARCERATED (current). Transplant clause has no lookback ('received or been advised to receive') -> ever. 'hospitalized within the last 3 months' -> HOSPITALIZED_MULTIPLE count_gte 1 within 3 months (same convention as transamerica uw.json).

rules.text: Does the Proposed Insured currently use a wheelchair due to a chronic illness or disease, or require assistance with activities of daily living such as bathing, dressing, eating or toileting?

Has the Proposed Insured been medically treated or diagnosed by a licensed member of the medical profession, or taken medication for: a. Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome (AIDS), AIDS Related Complex (ARC), or the Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV)?
rules.note: No lookback printed -> ever.

rules.text: Has the Proposed Insured been medically treated or diagnosed by a licensed member of the medical profession, or taken medication for: b. Alzheimer's, dementia, Lou Gehrig's Disease (ALS), Huntington's Disease, or prior to age 25, Cerebral Palsy, Down's Syndrome, spina bifida, cystic fibrosis, mental retardation, or muscular dystrophy?
rules.note: 'prior to age 25' qualifies only the second list (CP, Down's, spina bifida, CF, mental retardation, MD); read as diagnosed/treated before age 25. 'mental retardation' -> DOWN_SYNDROME (canonical label covers intellectual/developmental disability). SPINA_BIFIDA proposed. Onset of these conditions after 25 is not asked here (CF/MD later onset would only be caught by Rx).

rules.text: Has the Proposed Insured been medically treated or diagnosed by a licensed member of the medical profession, or taken medication for: c. A terminal medical condition that would reasonably be expected to cause death within the next 12 months?
rules.note: Threshold is 12 months life expectancy; canonical TERMINAL_ILLNESS is 12-24 months - capture life expectancy if the interview distinguishes.

rules.text: Has the Proposed Insured, within the past 12 months, been advised to have a diagnostic test, surgery, dialysis, home health care or hospitalization which has not yet been started, completed or for which results are not known?
rules.note: Covers advised-but-not-done dialysis/home health care/hospitalization as well as tests and surgery (canonical PENDING_TESTS).

rules.text: Within the past 2 years, has the Proposed Insured been medically treated or diagnosed by a licensed member of the medical profession, or taken medication for: a. Drug or alcohol dependency/habit or treatment for alcoholism or drug addiction or manic depression or schizophrenia?
rules.note: Part B header: 'if any question is answered "Yes," the Proposed Insured may be eligible for the Sentinel Plan New Vantage(R) III'. 'manic depression' -> BIPOLAR.

rules.text: Within the past 2 years, has the Proposed Insured been medically treated or diagnosed by a licensed member of the medical profession, or taken medication for: b. Heart attack, congestive heart failure, cardiomyopathy, stroke, Transient Ischemic Attack (TIA), aneurysm, or had heart or circulatory surgery?
rules.note: Surgery clause uses procedure date (basis diagnosed). Pacemaker/defibrillator included because the same application (Part C Q1a) defines heart surgery 'to include heart bypass, angioplasty, balloon procedure, stent placement or heart valve replacement, pacemaker/defibrillator'. Non-cardiac circulatory surgery (e.g., carotid endarterectomy, peripheral bypass) has no canonical code.

rules.text: Within the past 2 years, has the Proposed Insured been medically treated or diagnosed by a licensed member of the medical profession, or taken medication for: c. Treatment for insulin shock, diabetic coma, neuropathy, had an amputation or any other complication from diabetes?
rules.note: Read as a list of diabetic complications ('or any other complication from diabetes'): neuropathy -> DIABETIC_NEUROPATHY, amputation -> AMPUTATION_DISEASE; retinopathy/nephropathy/ulcers included as 'any other complication from diabetes'. Non-diabetic NEUROPATHY deliberately not mapped (see open_issues).

rules.text: Within the past 3 years, has the Proposed Insured been medically treated or diagnosed by a licensed member of the medical profession or taken medication for: brain tumor, internal cancer, malignant melanoma, leukemia or sickle cell anemia?
rules.note: 'internal cancer' -> CANCER/CANCER_METASTATIC/CANCER_RECURRENT/LYMPHOMA; SKIN_CANCER_BASAL not mapped (not internal).

rules.text: Within the past 5 years, has the Proposed Insured been diagnosed or treated by a licensed member of the medical profession or taken medication for: a. Coronary Artery Disease, heart attack, heart surgery to include heart bypass, angioplasty, balloon procedure, stent placement or heart valve replacement, pacemaker/defibrillator, stroke, aneurysm, angina, chest pain, or any other heart or circulatory disorder?
rules.note: Part C header: 'if any question is answered "Yes," the Proposed Insured may be eligible for the Sentinel Plan New Vantage(R) II'. 'any other heart or circulatory disorder' mapped to the remaining cardiac/vascular codes (CHF, cardiomyopathy, AFib, arrhythmia, valve disorder, PVD, clots, TIA, pulmonary hypertension). HYPERTENSION and HIGH_CHOLESTEROL deliberately NOT mapped although the literal wording could include them (see open_issues).

rules.text: Within the past 5 years, has the Proposed Insured been diagnosed or treated by a licensed member of the medical profession or taken medication for: b. Chronic disorder which requires the use of oxygen, or Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD), which includes emphysema, chronic asthma, or chronic bronchitis?
rules.note: Only CHRONIC asthma is asked; canonical ASTHMA does not distinguish mild/chronic - suppress for mild intermittent asthma if the interview captures severity.

rules.text: Within the past 5 years, has the Proposed Insured been diagnosed or treated by a licensed member of the medical profession or taken medication for: c. Parkinson's Disease, Kidney Disease, kidney failure, cirrhosis or other liver disease or any auto-immune disorder including Rheumatoid Arthritis, Systemic Lupus (SLE) or Sjogren's?
rules.note: 'any auto-immune disorder' mapped to RA, SLE, Sjogren's (named) plus scleroderma, MS and Crohn's/ulcerative colitis (commonly classed autoimmune/immune-mediated - mapping judgement) and proposed AUTOIMMUNE_OTHER. Hepatitis B/C included under 'other liver disease'.

rules.text: Within the past 5 years, has the Proposed Insured been diagnosed or treated by a licensed member of the medical profession or taken medication for: d. Diabetes treated by insulin more than 50 units daily?
rules.note: Needs daily insulin dose; extra predicate insulin_units_daily_gt is proposed (not in canonical extra_predicates). Insulin <= 50 units/day is not asked (consistent with guide Rx '*' footnote: rated only if > 50 units).

uw.routingText: Application with NV I, II & III (form SSLNV09-OT): any YES in Part A -> DECLINE (not eligible for any New Vantage plan); else any YES in Part B -> NV_III; else any YES in Part C -> NV_II; NO to all -> NV_I (subject to build chart and Rx lists in uw.json). WORST_OUTCOME over class_order [NV_I, NV_II, NV_III] + DECLINE reproduces this cascade exactly. State overrides (guide REV 08/20 p4): states without NV III (AR, MN, MT, NV) use the NV I & II application where Part A -> DECLINE, Part B -> NV_II, else NV_I (engine: remap NV_III -> NV_II there); MT uses an NV I-only application: Part A -> DECLINE, Part B -> submit to underwriting (REFER), else NV_I.

Current 07/26 product highlights also list a Premier risk class with a $10,000 minimum. The complete carrier Premier rate grid and carrier-authored Premier underwriting map were not located publicly, so Premier is intentionally NOT priced here.
Therefore a clean/low-risk applicant may receive a lower Premier premium from the live Transamerica eApp than this tool displays. The tool uses Select as the conservative best fully sourced class.

Current 2026 single-condition chart is highly permissive: conditions not represented by an adverse rule below default to Select. Carrier electronic medical/prescription data and the live application make the final decision.

Guide warns that multiple comorbidities may result in decline; this tool does not infer every possible clinical comorbidity pairing. Tobacco plus supplemental oxygen is specifically cited as an example requiring caution.

notes: 10-Pay Solution: level premiums for 10 years; issue ages 0-85 (age last birthday).
Issuer: Transamerica Life Insurance Company, Cedar Rapids, IA (all jurisdictions except NY); Transamerica Financial Life Insurance Company, Harrison, NY in New York (p28).
Policy Form # TPWL10IC-0818 or TPWL10-0818; 'Policy form and number may vary, and this product and riders may not be available in all jurisdictions' (p28).
Underwriting: real-time decision via iGO e-App using electronic medical/Rx data (Milliman); no exams or labs (p2, p4, p8).
Application valid 90 days; cases close after 45 days with outstanding requirements (p8).
Policy loans: rate variable, not to exceed 8% (p5). Matures at age 121 (p5).
Montana: Unisex-Male rates (rate chart footnote, p20/22/24/25/26).
Modal factors and policy fee are on the 'Calculating a Rate' page (p27), shown with an Immediate Solution example; the page is not product-scoped, so they are applied to all three products.
No face-amount increment stated; rates are per $1,000 unit.
Juvenile issue age 0 = 15 days to less than 1 year (juvenile build chart p17; CGR p7).

routing.note: p10 classes PREFERRED/STANDARD = Immediate Solution or 10-Pay Solution; GRADED = Easy Solution (case study 3, p19). Easy Solution issue ages 18-80, max face $25,000: a GRADED outcome at ages 0-17 or 81-85 has no product.

rules.text: Section 3.E: Have you ever been diagnosed by a member of the medical profession or tested positive for any of the following: Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome (AIDS), Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV), and/or tested positive on an AIDS/HIV related test?

rules.text: Section 6 OWNER: Is the Owner employed by any cannabis related business?

uw.routingText: Applies to the whole Final Expense Solutions portfolio (Immediate Solution, 10-Pay Solution, Easy Solution) - one application and one underwriting decision. Section 2 (upfront eligibility attestation): any listed condition -> DECLINE (ineligible for all three products). Sections 3.A/3.E/4/6: the application only collects facts and answer bands; the class comes from the carrier decision chart (outcomes copied here per band): PREFERRED or STANDARD -> Immediate Solution or 10-Pay Solution at that class; GRADED -> transamerica_easy_solution (ages 18-80, max $25,000; no product for GRADED at 0-17 or 81-85); DECLINE. Section 3.D checkboxes are screening only (outcome PREFERRED = no effect) and hand off to the uw.json GUIDE_RULE decision chart plus combination rules (two Standard/Graded conditions -> GRADED, four+ -> DECLINE, Standard condition + Standard build -> GRADED) and Activity Credit (3.E physical activity question). no_hits_outcome PREFERRED (subject to build, combination rules, electronic Rx/MIB data).

notes: Additional Benefits: None; Optional Riders: None (p5).
Rates sex-distinct only, no tobacco distinction (p26).
Issuer: Transamerica Life Insurance Company, Cedar Rapids, IA (all jurisdictions except NY); Transamerica Financial Life Insurance Company, Harrison, NY in New York (p28).
Policy Form # TPWL10IC-0818 or TPWL10-0818; 'Policy form and number may vary, and this product and riders may not be available in all jurisdictions' (p28).
Underwriting: real-time decision via iGO e-App using electronic medical/Rx data (Milliman); no exams or labs (p2, p4, p8).
Application valid 90 days; cases close after 45 days with outstanding requirements (p8).
Policy loans: rate variable, not to exceed 8% (p5). Matures at age 121 (p5).
Montana: Unisex-Male rates (rate chart footnote, p20/22/24/25/26).
Modal factors and policy fee are on the 'Calculating a Rate' page (p27), shown with an Immediate Solution example; the page is not product-scoped, so they are applied to all three products.
No face-amount increment stated; rates are per $1,000 unit.
Juvenile issue age 0 = 15 days to less than 1 year (juvenile build chart p17; CGR p7).

routing.note: p10 classes PREFERRED/STANDARD = Immediate Solution or 10-Pay Solution; GRADED = Easy Solution (case study 3, p19). Easy Solution issue ages 18-80, max face $25,000: a GRADED outcome at ages 0-17 or 81-85 has no product.

uw.routingText: Applies to the whole Final Expense Solutions portfolio (Immediate Solution, 10-Pay Solution, Easy Solution) - one application and one underwriting decision. Section 2 (upfront eligibility attestation): any listed condition -> DECLINE (ineligible for all three products). Sections 3.A/3.E/4/6: the application only collects facts and answer bands; the class comes from the carrier decision chart (outcomes copied here per band): PREFERRED or STANDARD -> Immediate Solution or 10-Pay Solution at that class; GRADED -> transamerica_easy_solution (ages 18-80, max $25,000; no product for GRADED at 0-17 or 81-85); DECLINE. Section 3.D checkboxes are screening only (outcome PREFERRED = no effect) and hand off to the uw.json GUIDE_RULE decision chart plus combination rules (two Standard/Graded conditions -> GRADED, four+ -> DECLINE, Standard condition + Standard build -> GRADED) and Activity Credit (3.E physical activity question). no_hits_outcome PREFERRED (subject to build, combination rules, electronic Rx/MIB data).

rules.text: Section 3.D: Have you ever been diagnosed, treated, tested positive for, or been given medical advice by a member of the medical profession for any of the following: (Select all that apply) Heart Disease
rules.note: Screening checkbox: a check does not by itself set the class; the e-App/underwriting places the case by the carrier decision chart (uw.json GUIDE_RULE rules for the same codes, e.g. CHF STANDARD, cancer within 2 yrs DECLINE). Outcome PREFERRED = no class effect from this rule alone (best class), so WORST_OUTCOME is unaffected; the code list tells the interview which chart rules/follow-ups to evaluate.

rules.text: Section 3.E: During the last 3 months, have you been on treatment for anemia (lower than normal number of red blood cells)? Include diet, iron pills, iron shots, infusions as treatment.
rules.note: Outcome from 12/23 chart: Anemia (other than Sickle Cell Anemia) treated within 3 months -> GRADED (routes to transamerica_easy_solution); with Activity Credit -> STANDARD (see uw.json activity_credit). ANEMIA is a proposed code (already proposed in transamerica uw.json).

rules.text: Section 3.E: In the last 12 months, were you a patient in a hospital overnight? (Do not include hospitalization due to child birth without complications or an overnight stay in an emergency room.)
rules.note: Outcome from 12/23 chart: Hospitalization within last 12 months -> STANDARD; with Activity Credit -> PREFERRED. Exclusions (uncomplicated childbirth, ER-only overnight) must be applied when capturing the count.

rules.text: Section 3.E: Have you ever been diagnosed by a member of the medical profession or tested positive for any of the following: Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome (AIDS), Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV), and/or tested positive on an AIDS/HIV related test?
rules.note: Chart: AIDS/HIV/ARC -> DECLINE.

rules.text: Section 4: Are you a U.S. citizen? Yes / No / Green Card (Green Card Number and Expiration Date; Country of Citizenship)
rules.note: Guide p4: underwriter referrals are limited to nonmedical risks incl. immigration status. A green-card holder (permanent resident) does not trigger; only non-citizen without permanent residency.

rules.text: Section 6 OWNER: Is the Owner employed by any cannabis related business?
rules.note: Asked of the Owner (who is usually the insured). Chart: Employment in the cannabis industry or a cannabis-related business -> DECLINE. CANNABIS_EMPLOYMENT is a proposed code (already proposed in transamerica uw.json). The paper form asks no separate cannabis question of the insured when insured != owner (not found in Section 1); the e-App may differ.
